Attempted all-GPU Metal pipeline: rmsNorm+GEMV batched with 2 syncs/layer. Native Metal MXFP4 E8M0+dynamic gs produces ~1% L2 drift per layer → NaN by L43. Root cause: GPU threadgroup parallel reduction uses different float rounding than CPU sequential sum. Reverted to CPU fallback for gemvMlxQ (bit-exact). Performance bottleneck remains: per-GEMV sync (~430 syncs per forward). The fix: need Metal GEMV kernel with EXACT float matching, or restructure to minimize CPU reads between Metal dispatches.

Multiple approaches tested: (1) Strategic syncs (4/layer vs 430) gives 0.8-0.9 tok/s but garbled (Metal rmsNorm drift). (2) Threaded CPU fallback: 28s (SLOWER — thread pool dispatch overhead for small matrices). (3) Threshold dispatch (>4096 threaded, else direct): 11s but still garbled. ROOT CAUSE: Metal rmsNorm produces different float values than CPU rmsNorm. Even tiny difference (0.3%) cascades through 43 layers to wrong first token. MUST use CPU rmsNorm for correctness. Need to find way to reduce sync count while using CPU rmsNorm.
